claim.why_it_matters: The centred, underlined general-format title that heads Format 2 and Format 3 of the CD entry is transcribed as a plain underlined paragraph, not a heading. The identical title on page 207, and every other general-format title in this batch (pages 205, 206, 209-216), is a '## ' heading, so this page's CD formats drop out of the document outline and heading-based slicing.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page 208 (folio V-16, rendered at 300 dpi) carries the centred, underlined title 'GENERAL FORMAT FOR COMMUNICATION DESCRIPTION ENTRY'. The markdown at specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md line 8669 carries the same words, underlined, in the same place, ahead of FORMAT 2. No text is missing or misquoted. The only difference is that the markdown has no '## ' heading marker, while page 207's identical title (line 8635) and most other general-format titles have one. The PDF has no heading levels to compare against, so this is a markdown formatting inconsistency that does not change meaning. The same convention gap also appears at lines 8181 (FILE CONTROL ENTRY) and 9891 (QUALIFICATION). It is a valid outline cleanup, but it is not a content discrepancy between the PDF and its transcription.
